description: Userspace can supply guest memory regions via KVM_SET_USER_MEMORY_REGION. Always present on modern kernels. Firecracker hard-requires this — without it there's no way to map guest RAM.
Extended memory-region API supporting guest_memfd-backed regions for confidential VMs. Optional; Firecracker uses standard KVM_SET_USER_MEMORY_REGION today.
In-kernel IRQ controller (PIC/IOAPIC on x86). Firecracker hard-requires this — userspace irqchip would push irq emulation cost back into VM exits.
Bind eventfd to MMIO/PIO write — short-circuits VirtIO doorbell exits. Required for low-overhead VirtIO.
Bind eventfd to GSI for in-kernel IRQ raise. Required for low-overhead VirtIO interrupt delivery.
Enables KVM_SIGNAL_MSI for direct MSI injection bypassing the routing table. Used by Firecracker for one-shot interrupts.
Lets userspace set the guest TSC frequency. Required for portable snapshots across hosts with different TSC frequencies. Snapshot restore on a host without this fails if the recorded TSC differs.
Returns the size (bytes) of the dynamic XSAVE buffer for KVM_GET_XSAVE2 / KVM_SET_XSAVE2. Required for AVX-512 / AMX state. Firecracker queries this once at vCPU init.
Recommended max vCPUs per VM. Firecracker caps user-requested vcpu_count at this value. (KVM_CAP_MAX_VCPUS is the hard limit.)
Hard maximum vCPUs per VM. Firecracker's machine_config caps vcpu_count at min(this, 32) per its design constraints.
Required by Intel VT-x for its TSS area. Firecracker calls KVM_SET_TSS_ADDR(0xfffbd000) at VM init. Absent on AMD-only kernels (AMD doesn't need TSS area).
Number of hardware breakpoints supported via KVM_SET_GUEST_DEBUG. The GDB stub queries this to know the breakpoint budget.
Per-vCPU ring buffer of dirtied page indices — alternative to KVM_GET_DIRTY_LOG bitmap. Lower latency for sparse-write workloads. Optional; Firecracker uses the bitmap path by default.
Decouples dirty-log read from write-protect (no auto-clear on KVM_GET_DIRTY_LOG). Required for the two-phase dirty tracking pattern (read, persist, then KVM_CLEAR_DIRTY_LOG).

x86-only. Lets userspace ask KVM not to take exits for HLT/MWAIT/PAUSE/CSTATE — the guest's wait instructions are passed to the host CPU directly. Used for latency-sensitive workloads. Firecracker can opt in via the cpu-template configuration.
ARM-only. Max guest physical address space size in bits. Firecracker encodes this into the VM type when calling KVM_CREATE_VM on aarch64.
